To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) The use of big and open linked data (BOLD), as a new economic resource, is a new and exciting development.
(1) The value of data is seldom realized on their own.
BOLD offers a new opportunity to break through the current limits of backward induction by moving back and forth to explore the unknown.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions. What are the different types of BOLD and how are they related to one another? How do we make sense out of the data? What is the value of BOLD in research, policy and practice?
the development of a new approach to BOLD that can help us understand the nature and value of data, and how to make use of it in the research process.

how BOLD can be applied to research, policy, practice, and education, in the following ways: (1) BOLD can be used to generate new insights and knowledge in research; (2) BOLD can provide evidence to support the development of new policies; (3) BOLD can inform and enhance the delivery of new practices; and (4) BOLD can help to develop a new generation of researchers, policy makers, and practitioners.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BOLD is a new frontier in the social sciences and humanities, and that it is an important area of study that requires a new set of theories and methods.
the BOLD approach offers a new way of thinking and a new way of doing research in the digital era.
BOLD is not a panacea to the problems of data analysis, but it is a powerful tool for data-driven research, policy, or practice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of big and open linked data in research, policy and practice requires a new approach to the research and development process.
the BOLD is not just a new data set or a new technology, it is a new way of doing research and policy.
we are developing a theory of big and open linked data (BOLD).
The main takeaway from our work is that

we need to move away from the traditional data driven approaches to BOLD, and to adopt a more interdisciplinary and multi-methods approach to BOLD to better understand its potential and to maximize the benefits of BOLD.
we need to develop a variety of rigorous methods to counterbalance the theory-free practice in the analysis of BOLD.
the analysis of BOLD requires a more rigorous approach that is informed by theories and methods from diverse disciplines.
